examples.en: I saw a knight's armor from long ago at the museum.
Armor is heavy, so it is hard to wear for long.

examples.ko: 영화 주인공이 은색 갑옷을 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie appeared in silver armor.
The armor got dented when the sword hit it.

examples.ko: 아이가 종이로 갑옷 모양 옷을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child made an armor-shaped outfit out of paper.
It is dangerous to fight without armor.

explain: 갑옷은 '입다'와 함께 쓰고, 몸 전체를 감싸는 옛날 쇠 옷을 떠올리면 돼요. 가슴만 막는 '방탄조끼'와는 달라요. 요즘은 역사, 게임, 영화 이야기에서 주로 들어요.
explain_en: 갑옷 goes with the verb 입다 and brings to mind the old metal suit that covers the whole body. It differs from a 방탄조끼 (bulletproof vest), which protects only the chest. Today you mostly hear it in talk about history, games, and movies.

examples.ko: 저는 광대뼈가 높아서 사진이 잘 나와요.
examples.en: I have high cheekbones, so I look good in photos.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 광대뼈 위에 볼터치를 해요.
examples.en: When I do makeup, I put blush on top of my cheekbones.
I fell and hurt my cheekbone.
When you smile, the cheekbone area lifts up.
He has a face with prominent cheekbones.
The cheekbone is right below the eye.

explain: 말할 때는 '광대'라고 줄여서 '광대가 나왔다'처럼 말하기도 해요. '광대뼈가 나오다', '광대뼈가 튀어나오다'처럼 얼굴 모양을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: In speech people sometimes shorten it to '광대', as in '광대가 나왔다'. It often appears when describing face shape, as in '광대뼈가 나오다' or '광대뼈가 튀어나오다'.

examples.en: I didn't want to do my homework, so I pretended to be sick.

examples.ko: 꾀병인 줄 알았는데 진짜 열이 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought he was faking it, but he really had a fever.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교에 안 가려고 꾀병을 부리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling seems to be faking illness to skip school.

examples.ko: 꾀병 부리지 말고 어서 일어나서 준비해요.
examples.en: Stop faking being sick and get up and get ready.
Mom quickly figured out that I was faking.

examples.ko: 시험 날만 되면 배가 아프다니 꾀병 아니에요?
examples.en: Your stomach only hurts on exam days? Aren't you faking it?

explain: 보통 '꾀병을 부리다'로 말해요. 진짜 아픈 사람에게 '꾀병이야'라고 하면 크게 실례가 되니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '꾀병을 부리다'. Be careful: telling someone who is truly sick '꾀병이야' is very rude.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my body is shivering.
My hands trembled with fear.

examples.ko: 겨울 바람 속에서 덜덜 떨며 버스를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited for the bus, shivering in the winter wind.

examples.ko: 시험 전에는 다리가 덜덜 떨릴 만큼 긴장돼요.
examples.en: Before the exam, I'm so nervous that my legs shake.

examples.ko: 낡은 세탁기가 덜덜 소리를 내며 돌아가요.
examples.en: The old washing machine runs with a rattling noise.
He spoke while trembling.

explain: 추위나 무서움 때문에 몸이 크게 떨리는 모양이에요. 보통 '덜덜 떨다, 덜덜 떨리다'로 써요. '달달'은 더 작고 가볍게 떠는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body shaking hard from cold or fear, usually as '덜덜 떨다' or '덜덜 떨리다'. '달달' gives a smaller, lighter shaking feel.

examples.en: Thick socks are nice in winter.
My younger sibling has full lips, so they look cute.
This notebook has nicely thick paper.
I grilled thickly sliced meat.
The blanket is thick, so it will be warm.
The cardigan was thick but not heavy.

explain: '두껍다'는 그냥 두께가 있다는 뜻이고, '도톰하다'는 적당히 두꺼워서 따뜻하거나 보기 좋다는 느낌이 있어요. 옷, 입술, 고기, 종이에 자주 써요. 너무 두꺼울 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 두껍다 just says something has thickness, while 도톰하다 suggests it is moderately thick in a nice or cozy way. It is common for clothes, lips, meat and paper, but not for something excessively thick.

examples.en: My cold was bad, so I got an IV drip.
I fell asleep while getting the IV drip.

examples.ko: 링거 바늘을 꽂을 때 아파서 얼굴을 찡그렸어요.
examples.en: It hurt when the IV needle went in, so I frowned.
The IV bottle is almost empty.
After getting the drip, I felt energized.
The nurse swapped in a new IV bag.

explain: '링거를 맞다'라고 하고 '먹다'를 쓰지 않아요. 원래는 수액의 한 종류 이름인데 한국에서는 팔에 꽂는 수액 주사를 통틀어 '링거'라고 해요. 병원에서 쓰는 정확한 말은 '수액'이에요.
explain_en: You say '링거를 맞다', never '먹다'. It was originally the name of one type of IV fluid, but in Korea '링거' covers any IV drip into the arm. The more exact hospital term is '수액'.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.

examples.ko: 엄마가 손으로 짠 머플러를 선물해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mom gave me a scarf she knitted by hand.
In winter, just one scarf keeps you warm.

examples.ko: 이 빨간 머플러는 어느 코트에나 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This red scarf goes well with any coat.
My scarf almost blew away in the wind.
I left my scarf on the subway.

explain: 목에 두르는 목도리를 말하고, 일상에서는 '목도리'가 더 흔해요. '머플러'는 패션 쪽에서 조금 멋을 내는 느낌으로 써요. 자동차 배기 장치를 뜻하는 '머플러'도 있어서 문맥으로 구분해요.
explain_en: It means a neck scarf, but 목도리 is more common in daily life. 머플러 sounds a bit more fashionable. 머플러 can also mean a car's exhaust muffler, so context tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: I got athlete's foot, so I'm putting medicine on it.

examples.ko: 무좀은 따뜻하고 습한 곳에서 잘 번져요.
examples.en: Athlete's foot spreads easily in warm, humid places.

examples.ko: 무좀 때문에 발가락 사이가 계속 가려워요.
examples.en: Because of athlete's foot, the area between my toes keeps itching.

examples.ko: 무좀에 걸린 가족과 수건을 따로 써야 해요.
examples.en: You should use separate towels from a family member with athlete's foot.
I'd had athlete's foot for a long time, so I went to the hospital.
After applying the athlete's foot medicine, it got much better.

explain: '무좀에 걸리다', '무좀이 생기다'처럼 말하고, 약은 '무좀약'이라고 해요. 증상은 주로 가려움이라서 '발이 가렵다'와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People say '무좀에 걸리다' or '무좀이 생기다', and the medicine is called '무좀약'. Itching is the typical symptom, so it often comes up together with '발이 가렵다'.

examples.en: I shaved my head before going into the army.
After shaving my head, it felt cool.
He decided to shave his head to become a monk.
A cap suits a shaved head well.
I saw my son with a shaved head for the first time.

examples.ko: 야구부 학생들은 시즌 전에 삭발을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball team students shave their heads before the season.

explain: 삭발은 머리를 거의 밀어 버릴 때 쓰고, 보통 머리를 자를 때는 '이발'이나 '커트'를 써요. '삭발을 하다'로 말하고, 군대, 운동부, 스님, 굳은 각오를 보여 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 삭발 is for shaving the head almost bald, while an ordinary haircut is '이발' or '커트'. You say '삭발을 하다'. It often comes up with the army, sports teams, monks, or showing strong resolve.

examples.en: I got a chest X-ray at the hospital.
There was no problem on the X-ray.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 엑스레이 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me the X-ray image.
At the dentist I had an X-ray taken and then got treatment.

examples.ko: 엑스레이가 나오려면 십 분쯤 기다려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to wait about ten minutes for the X-ray.
At the airport they check bags with an X-ray.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. 사진을 찍는 것처럼 '찍다'를 쓰는 게 특징이에요. 더 정확한 검사인 'CT'나 'MRI'와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: At the hospital you say 엑스레이를 찍다, using 찍다 (take a photo) with it. It often appears together with the more detailed scans CT and MRI.

examples.en: I ate spoiled food and got gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염 때문에 이틀 동안 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of gastroenteritis, I ate only porridge for two days.
The doctor said it was acute gastroenteritis.
I stayed home from school until the gastroenteritis cleared up.
The child had a fever and vomited from gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염은 손을 자주 씻으면 예방할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can prevent gastroenteritis by washing your hands often.

explain: 위와 장에 염증이 생겨 배가 아프고 토하거나 설사하는 병이에요. 보통 '위장염에 걸리다'로 말해요. '위장병'은 넓은 말이고 '위장염'은 염증이 있는 병이에요.
explain_en: It is an illness where the stomach and intestines are inflamed, causing stomach pain, vomiting or diarrhea. It is usually said as '위장염에 걸리다'. '위장병' is a broad term, while '위장염' is specifically an inflammation.

examples.en: I got a call from the hospital telling me to come in for a retest.
The result was unclear, so they say a retest is needed.
The retest results come out next week.
I went back to the hospital for a retest.
The retest came back normal, so I was relieved.
Does a retest cost money again?

explain: '재검사를 받다', '재검사를 하다'처럼 써요. 건강검진뿐 아니라 제품 품질 검사나 시험에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 병원 이야기에서 가장 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It is used as '재검사를 받다' or '재검사를 하다'. It also applies to product quality checks and exams, but in daily life you meet it most often in talk about hospitals.

examples.ko: 할머니의 주치의 선생님은 같은 병원에 오래 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother's regular doctor has been at the same hospital for a long time.
Before the surgery I consulted in detail with my doctor.
My doctor suggested changing the medicine.
The president has a dedicated personal physician.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 이 병원 의사 선생님이 주치의예요.
examples.en: Since I was little, the doctor at this clinic has been my regular doctor.

examples.ko: 주치의는 환자의 건강을 오랫동안 살펴 주는 사람이에요.
examples.en: A regular doctor looks after the patient's health over a long time.

explain: 한 사람의 병을 계속 맡아서 살펴보는 의사예요. 입원했을 때 맡은 의사는 '담당 의사'라고도 하는데, '주치의'는 더 오랜 관계의 느낌이 있어요. '우리 주치의'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A doctor who keeps looking after one person's health. A hospital doctor in charge is also called 담당 의사, but 주치의 suggests a longer relationship. People say it like 우리 주치의.

examples.en: These pants are a bit tight at the waist.

examples.ko: 이번 주 일정이 너무 타이트해서 쉴 틈이 없어요.
examples.en: This week's schedule is so tight that I have no time to rest.
A tight shirt is uncomfortable to move in.

examples.ko: 올해는 예산이 타이트해서 큰 행사는 어려워요.
examples.en: The budget is tight this year, so a big event is difficult.
The jeans got tighter after washing.
The deadline was tight, but the team pulled it off.

explain: 옷은 '꽉 끼다', 일정과 예산은 '빠듯하다'라고 해도 돼요. 타이트하다는 외래어라 직장이나 패션 이야기에서 특히 자주 들려요. 반대는 옷이면 '헐렁하다', 일정이면 '여유 있다'예요.
explain_en: For clothes you can say 꽉 끼다 and for schedules or budgets 빠듯하다 instead. 타이트하다 is a loanword that you hear especially in work and fashion talk. The opposite is 헐렁하다 for clothes and 여유 있다 for schedules.

examples.en: The groom was wearing a black tuxedo.
People usually wear a bow tie with a tuxedo.

examples.ko: 턱시도는 파티나 결혼식 같은 큰 행사에 입어요.
examples.en: A tuxedo is worn at big events such as parties or weddings.
A photo of a cat in a tuxedo pattern was popular.
He is a person who looks good in a tuxedo.
It is fine to wear a suit instead of a tuxedo.

explain: '정장'은 면접이나 회사에서 입는 양복이고, 턱시도는 결혼식이나 시상식 같은 격식 있는 저녁 행사에 입는 예복이에요. 검은 털과 하얀 털이 섞인 고양이를 '턱시도 고양이'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: 정장 is the suit worn to interviews or the office, while a 턱시도 is formal wear for formal evening events such as weddings or award ceremonies. A cat with mixed black and white fur is also called a '턱시도 고양이'.
